clue.text: A joint is essential when backing English group diet

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the synonym for the word before it is written from its end

blocks.note: a leg is a joint of meat
taken as written
essential means vital
E is the abbreviation for English
a body is a group of people

explanation.surface: A cannabis smoker's habit is central to the eating plan of an English group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' looks like food, but here it is the name of a parliament, as in the Japanese Diet or the medieval Diet of Worms.
explanation.definitionFit: A Diet is a formal national assembly that makes laws, the name used for several parliaments.

clue.text: One moves, but it could be sore if lacking support

indicators.note: could be suggests the word given is only one possible arrangement of its letters, which may be another

blocks.note: a prop is a support
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone moves house, but it could be painful without a supporting hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: take the support away from the answer and what remains is a rearrangement of sore.
explanation.definitionFit: In a debate the person who moves a motion formally puts it forward, and is called its proposer.

clue.text: Any king is bound to be cross

indicators.note: something bound is tied up inside, so one word is held within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
GR, Georgius Rex, is King George

explanation.surface: Any monarch put in chains will certainly be in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective is an everyday synonym for annoyed or in a bad temper.

clue.text: Domain of sly, cruel cook

definitions.note: with 'of ... cook' the whole clue reads as the place a cook works

indicators.note: to cook something is to doctor or falsify it, as with books, so the letters are tampered with

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The kitchen is the realm of a sly and cruel cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as the person whose domain this is, but it is the verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery is the back kitchen for washing up, the working territory of kitchen staff.

clue.text: Bernard's declining to whimper

indicators.note: in a down entry declining means going downward from the end, so the name is read upward

blocks.note: Bernard Levin was a well-known British newspaper columnist and critic

explanation.surface: Bernard is refusing, in a sulky way, to whine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declining' seems to mean refusing; in a down clue it means the letters run the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to cry or complain in a weak, sniffing, tearful way, much like whimpering.

clue.text: One is apt to be driven

definitions.text: One is apt to be driven

blocks.clueFragment: One is apt to be driven
blocks.note: surface reading: someone prone to being pushed hard or compelled
setter's reading: someone who travels in a car steered by another

explanation.walkthrough: Driven sounds like ambitious or compelled; here it simply means carried in a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller riding in a car, bus or taxi, not at the wheel, is carried about by whoever steers.

clue.text: Wealthy type gets model to strip

blocks.note: Dives is the rich man in the Bible parable of Lazarus
the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: A rich man hires a model to undress for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives, the traditional name for the rich man in Luke's parable, is a crossword favourite for a wealthy person.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to take off clothing or remove possessions, the same as stripping someone of them.

clue.text: After dancing in clogs, drinks up and all must go

indicators.note: dancing feet move about, so these letters are shuffled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
to drink up is to down ale, read as downs ale

explanation.surface: After a clog dance the performers drink up and everyone has to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All must go' sounds like last orders at the pub; it is the shop-window slogan of a business selling off its stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything must go is the standard advertising cry of a shop clearing its stock before it shuts.

clue.text: Two Good Friday participants against a scheme for peace?

blocks.note: Eire and NI (Northern Ireland) were parties to the 1998 Good Friday peace agreement
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Two signatories to the Good Friday deal oppose a plan for peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Good Friday here is the 1998 Belfast Agreement, not the Easter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: An eirenicon is a proposal put forward to reconcile opponents, from the Greek word for peace.

clue.text: Tempestuous character - one found in Lear, perhaps

indicators.note: found in says one item is placed inside the following word
perhaps hints that the result is only one possible arrangement, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: King Lear, taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A stormy character, someone like King Lear perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempestuous' sounds like stormy, as Lear is; it means belonging to Shakespeare's play The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy spirit who serves Prospero in Shakespeare's play The Tempest.

clue.text: Like Britain's past glory without a hazard

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter named after it is dropped

blocks.note: Britain's past glory was its empire
taken as written

explanation.surface: Like the vanished days of the British Empire, without any risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To hazard something, as a verb, is to put it at risk or endanger it.

clue.text: Piano serves to transform the office

indicators.note: to transform is to change the form of something, so the letters are recast

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piano is used to brighten up the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The office' looks like a workplace; in church language an office is a set service of daily prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening service of the Divine Office, the cycle of daily church prayers.

clue.text: Girl from classical Greece

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the word that follows, sitting inside it

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word
surface padding that completes the ancient-world picture

explanation.surface: A young woman from the world of ancient Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a young woman.

clue.text: General service footwear

blocks.note: first meaning: the Duke who beat Napoleon at Waterloo
second meaning: a rubber boot, named after a style of military boot

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as general-issue army boots; General is the soldier, and the boots are named after him. A wellington is the British name for a rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington was the great British general, and the boot styled for him became the wellington.

clue.text: Scrooge is broke without a couple of bob, or less

indicators.note: less means minus, so the letters just before it are taken away
without in its old sense of outside, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: skint is British slang for having no money
a florin was an old British coin worth two shillings, two bob
taken as written

explanation.surface: Scrooge is penniless without even two shillings, or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here has its old meaning of outside, so the slang word for broke wraps round the shortened coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge, Dickens's miser, gave his name to any mean, money-hoarding person.

clue.text: Screw holds a number in bird

indicators.note: in places the thing just named inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a turkey is a bird
n is the mathematical symbol for a number

explanation.surface: A prison officer keeps an inmate locked up doing time.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is British slang for a prison warder and bird is slang for prison time, so the surface is pure jail talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is an old word for a jailer, the person who holds the cell keys, as is screw in slang.

clue.text: A palm may be, as in cupidity

indicators.note: in places the small word inside the word that follows it

blocks.note: cupidity is greed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's palm might be crossed, as happens where there is avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: To grease someone's palm is to bribe them, which fits the greed in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom to grease a palm means to bribe, so a bribed hand is described as greased.

clue.text: Keillor's defence?

definitions.note: not a definition so much as a reference to the man's first name

blocks.note: first meaning: the given name of ... Keillor, the American radio humorist
second meaning: troops stationed to protect a town or fort

explanation.walkthrough: Keillor is the host of the radio show A Prairie Home Companion; the question mark flags the play on his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is the body of soldiers posted to guard a fortress, which serves as its protection.

clue.text: Al Gore is unlikely to keep concubines

definitions.note: the answer is a place for keeping them

indicators.note: unlikely suggests something improbable or odd, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The former US Vice President is hardly the type to maintain mistresses.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the women's quarters of a Turkish palace, a harem where wives and mistresses lived.

clue.text: Offers to play lovers' tune

indicators.note: to play is to perform or muck about with, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician offers to perform a romantic song.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer is to put oneself forward freely, the same as making an offer to do something.

clue.text: Killing is all the rage!

indicators.note: rage is wild, uncontrolled fury, so the letters before it are thrown about

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Murder has become the latest fashion!
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the rage' reads as a single idiom for fashionable; split it so 'rage' acts on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing as an adjective means deadly or fatal, which is exactly what this word means.

clue.text: He may feel destined to succeed in part

definitions.text: He may feel destined to succeed

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the words before it is used, a run of their letters

blocks.note: the run of letters sitting across these two words

explanation.surface: Someone believes fate has marked him for success in some role.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of the first part doubles as the definition, since the firstborn son traditionally inherits.
explanation.definitionFit: Under primogeniture the firstborn son is the heir expected to inherit title and estate.

clue.text: Dunkirk began fightback from a no-win situation

indicators.note: began points to the opening of the place name, its first letter only
the back half of this compound says the synonym for its front half is turned round and read the other way

blocks.note: the first letter of the town's name
a war is a fight

explanation.surface: At Dunkirk the British began to fight back out of a hopeless position.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is hidden inside the single word fightback: fight gives the letters, back turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn game ends level, with neither side winning, so it is a result without a victor.

clue.text: Odds and ends singularly unappealing to 15

definitions.note: describes the verb rather than defining it: something a miser hates doing

indicators.note: singularly asks for the plural word before it to be put into its one-of form

blocks.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds at the start of a race
the singular of ends

explanation.surface: Bits and pieces are particularly unattractive to a miser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds and ends' wants to be one phrase for bits and pieces; split it. 15 is SKINFLINT, the miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hates parting with money, so laying out cash is exactly the activity that repels him.

clue.text: Outre student found in bed, the worse for drink

indicators.note: found in places the words before it inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
OTT, over the top, means outrageous
L for learner, a student

explanation.surface: An outrageous student is discovered in bed, drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottled is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottled is a British slang word for drunk, just as being the worse for drink means intoxicated.

clue.text: Calls in question politician using spin

indicators.note: spin means twisting or rotating, so the letters are whirled into a new order

blocks.note: MP, Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone challenges a politician who relies on media spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' looks like political PR, the noun; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn is to challenge the truth or honesty of a claim, to cast doubt on it.

clue.text: There's many a drop down here

definitions.text: There's many a drop down here

blocks.note: d is a standard abbreviation for down
rain is a great many drops of water

explanation.surface: A sheer cliff edge where there are many steep falls.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and its words also build the answer: the short form of down follows the many drops.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe or channel carrying away rainwater and waste swallows countless drops of liquid.

clue.text: Charge for a snog with a bird?

blocks.note: to spoon is old slang for kissing and cuddling
a bill is a charge

explanation.surface: Paying for a kiss with a girlfriend, bird being British slang for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The spoonbill is a wading bird with a long flat beak that widens at the tip like a spoon.
